rows.behavior: Dry-run mode leaves file contents and existence unchanged for creation, deletion, updates, and moves.

fix.defect: The reconstruction's delete-move-and-dry-run-defects section and patch-lifecycle.json reproduce deletion of both DELETE targets and MOVE sources during dry-run.
fix.intent: aider/args.py:512 promises: Perform a dry run without modifying files (default: False).
fix.behavior: Suppress every file mutation in dry-run, including direct touches, directory creation, deletion, destination writes, and move-source unlink. Preserve the existing source and destination contents.

rows.behavior: Nonempty architect replies ask whether to edit unless automatic acceptance is enabled; blank replies do not start an editor.
The architect uses the configured editor model or falls back to its main model, with the main model's editor edit format.
The editor receives the architect reply as a fresh request with preprocessing disabled and both conversation-history lists cleared.
The editor inherits file context but disables suggested shell commands, prompt caching, cache warming, and format-change summarization.
Architect edits use the editor's ordinary format application rather than a separate atomic application step.
After the editor finishes, its assistant commit hashes are assigned back to the architect coder.
The editor starts with the architect's total cost and returns its accumulated total after the editor request finishes.
The architect disables repository-map tokens for its editor request.
Context mode forces map refresh, multiplies the map budget by the no-file multiplier, and resets that multiplier to one.
Context replies replace editable files with mentioned files and request another reply unless the selection is unchanged or the reflection count reaches the stopping threshold.
Context completion returns before ordinary edit application, including for blank replies.
Text reads use the configured codec and universal-newline handling, with Aider-equivalent read results and error diagnostics.
Text writes overwrite the target using the configured codec and newline policy, including strict encoding failures.
Permission-denied writes retry up to five attempts with exponential delays before reporting and raising; other OS errors report and raise immediately.
tests: test/working-tree.test.ts::reports a write failure when the parent directory is missing

rows.behavior: Writes do not use temporary-file replacement, fsync, or multi-file transactions; an earlier successful write survives a later failure.
SEARCH, divider, and REPLACE markers are recognized on stripped lines with five to nine marker characters, an optional ">" after SEARCH, and trailing whitespace.
A reply yields one (filename, SEARCH text, REPLACE text) edit per SEARCH/REPLACE block in reply order, with each text taken verbatim between its markers.
REPLACE text ends at a REPLACE marker or at another divider line, whichever comes first.
A block without its divider, or without a closing REPLACE or divider line, fails parsing with an error that shows the reply up to that line, a "^^^" pointer, and the expected marker.
A block with no recoverable filename and no earlier block filename fails with "Bad/missing filename. The filename must be alone on the line before the opening fence" and the fence.

The filename comes from the up to three lines before a SEARCH marker, continuing past fence lines, with fences carrying a path-like tag, trailing colons, leading hashes, backticks, and asterisks stripped, and "..." never a filename.
Among filename candidates, an exact in-chat name wins, then an in-chat basename match, then one difflib close match at cutoff 0.8, then the first candidate containing a dot, then the first candidate.
A block whose preceding lines yield no filename reuses the filename of the previous block in the same reply.
A block with an empty SEARCH section keeps its literal filename instead of being matched to in-chat names, so a new file is not remapped to a similar existing file.
A fence tagged bash, sh, shell, cmd, batch, powershell, ps1, zsh, fish, ksh, csh, or tcsh becomes a suggested shell command instead of an edit unless a SEARCH marker begins one or two lines after it.
SEARCH and REPLACE texts drop a first line ending in the target file name and an enclosing fence pair, and nonempty results end with a newline.
An empty or whitespace-only SEARCH appends the REPLACE text to the current file content, or starts the content of a new file, and never overwrites existing content.
Nonempty file content, SEARCH text, and REPLACE text each gain a trailing newline before matching, so a file without a final newline gains one after an edit.
Matching first tries an exact contiguous run of whole lines and replaces only the first matching run, without requiring the SEARCH text to be unique.

Without an exact match, SEARCH and REPLACE lose their minimum common leading whitespace, the first run of file lines equal after lstrip whose nonblank lines share one extra prefix is replaced, and that prefix is added to nonblank REPLACE lines.
A SEARCH of more than two lines whose first line is blank is retried without that line, with exact and whitespace-tolerant matching.

SEARCH and REPLACE split on standalone "..." lines must pair piece for piece with identical delimiters; each nonempty SEARCH piece must occur exactly once and is replaced once in order, an empty SEARCH piece appends its REPLACE piece, and any mismatch fails the block.
A SEARCH that matches no lines exactly, after whitespace repair, blank-line retry, or ellipsis pieces fails, even when similar lines exist.

When a nonempty SEARCH fails in its named file, the editable chat files are tried in set iteration order and the first file where it matches becomes the edit target, during preflight and during application.

Unmatched blocks fail with one error that lists each failed block and its SEARCH/REPLACE text, similar file lines at a 0.6 similarity ratio, a note when the REPLACE text is already present, the exact-match reminder, and, when other blocks applied, an instruction not to resend them.
Blocks apply in reply order, each reading the file after earlier blocks were written, and blocks that matched stay written when a later block fails.
Preflight resolves each block against the files on disk without writing and without applying earlier blocks, and returns each edit with its resolved target path for authorization.

Whole-file parsing reads the combined content of the reply and its continuations, a line starting with either fence string opens or closes a file block, and the lines inside a block become that file's complete new content with no search or merge.

A file block takes its filename from the line just before its opening fence, stripped of asterisks, a trailing colon, backticks, leading hashes, and whitespace, and a candidate longer than 250 characters is discarded.
A block filename that is not an in-chat file but whose basename is an in-chat relative filename is replaced by that basename.

A block without a usable filename uses the last backtick-quoted in-chat filename named in the prose since the previous block, then the only in-chat file, and otherwise fails with "No filename provided before <fence> in file listing".
A file block still open at the end of the reply becomes an edit with the lines received so far.
Whole-file edits are kept in the order of filename provenance (explicit block name, then prose mention, then sole chat file), and only the first edit for each filename is applied.
Applying a whole-file edit overwrites the target with the joined block lines, including empty content.

An edit to a missing path asks "Create new file?" for that path; a decline prints "Skipping edits to <path>" and drops its edits, and approval creates the empty file outside dry-run and adds it to the editable chat set.

An edit to an existing file outside the chat asks "Allow edits to file that has not been added to the chat?"; a decline prints "Skipping edits to <path>" and drops its edits, and approval adds the file to the editable chat set.

Before each request the fence is the first of the fence pairs ```, ````, <source>, <code>, <pre>, <codeblock>, and <sourcecode> whose opening or closing string starts no line of the editable or read-only file content, falling back to ``` with a warning.
Unified-diff parsing reads only fenced blocks whose opening line starts with ```diff, each ending at the next line that starts with ```, after a final newline is added to the reply.
Leading "--- " and "+++ " lines name the file by the +++ path, dropping its "b/" prefix only when the --- path starts with "a/" or is /dev/null, and keeping spaces in the path.
"@@" lines end hunks without their line numbers being read, and a hunk with no "+" or "-" line is discarded.
A hunk parsed without a filename takes the last filename seen earlier in the reply.
A "--- " and "+++ " pair inside a diff block starts the next file with the +++ path taken verbatim, without "b/" stripping.
Before application each hunk is rebuilt as a full-context diff with whitespace-only lines reduced to their line ending, and an identical path and normalized hunk is applied only once.
A hunk whose before text is empty or whitespace-only appends its after text to the file, creating a missing file.

A hunk first applies by literal replacement of its before text with its after text, tried unchanged, with outer blank lines stripped, in relative indentation, and both, converting a relative-indentation result back to absolute indentation.

When direct replacement fails, the before text is rebuilt from the file through diff-match-patch line diffing, and the rebuilt text is used only if it keeps at least ten non-whitespace characters and two thirds of the original before lines.

A hunk that still fails applies change section by change section, each with adjacent context reduced one line at a time from all of it to none, preferring more preceding context at each size, and fails if any section fails.
Literal replacement changes every occurrence of the before text, except that a before text with fewer than ten non-whitespace characters that occurs more than once is not replaced.
Unified-diff application never tries the diff-match-patch, git cherry-pick, or reverse-line strategies kept in search_replace.py, and SEARCH/REPLACE never uses search_replace.py.
Hunks apply in order, each successful hunk is written at once, and failed hunks are collected into one error raised after the rest, so earlier writes survive.
A hunk that cannot apply is reported as "UnifiedDiffNoMatch: hunk failed to apply!" with the file name and the before lines that were not found in a row.
When some hunks applied and others failed, the failure message ends with "Note: some hunks did apply successfully. See the updated source code shown above."

fix.defect: The note is added only when the joined error string is shorter in characters than the number of hunks, so it is almost never shown. The reconstruction calls this a source-confirmed reporting defect (aider/coders/udiff_coder.py:88-118).
fix.intent: The other_hunks_applied message (aider/coders/udiff_coder.py:41-43) says "some hunks did apply successfully", and the guard compares against len(uniq), the number of hunks attempted, so the check was meant to count failed hunks against attempted hunks.
fix.behavior: Append the note whenever the number of failed hunks is less than the number of hunks attempted.

rows.behavior: A patch reply whose first line starts with "*** Begin Patch" is parsed to "*** End Patch"; a reply without that first line but with "@@" or Add, Update, or Delete File headers is parsed from its first line after a missing-sentinel warning, and any other reply yields no edits and "Response does not appear to be in patch format."
Parsing reads every Update and Delete target from disk before authorization and fails with "File referenced in patch not found or could not be read: <path>" when a target cannot be read.

"*** Add File:", "*** Update File:" with an optional following "*** Move to:", and "*** Delete File:" lines start actions, a header without a path fails, blank lines between actions are skipped, and any other line fails with "Unknown or misplaced line while parsing patch".

A repeated Update of a file adds its chunks to the first Update, a different second Move to target fails, a repeated Delete is ignored with a warning, and any other repeated or conflicting action for a path fails.
A patch parse failure is reported as "Error parsing patch content: <reason>" and handled as a malformed reply.
Add File content keeps each "+" line without its prefix and each blank line as an empty line, joins them with LF, and fails on any other line with "Invalid Add File line (missing '+')".

In an Update section, " " lines are context, "-" lines are deletions that also count as original context, "+" lines are insertions that do not, blank lines are context, and any other prefix or a stray "***" line fails.

"@@ <text>" scope lines must match consecutive stripped file lines at or after the current position, retried against stripped scope text with one fuzz, move the position past them, and fail with "Could not find scope context" when absent.
Section context is found at or after the current position by exact lines (fuzz 0), then right-stripped lines (fuzz 1), then stripped lines (fuzz 100), each pass taking the first occurrence.
A section ending with "*** End of File" first matches its context at the end of the file, then falls back to the forward search with 10,000 added fuzz.
Context that cannot be found fails with "Could not find patch context" naming the line it searched from and listing the context lines.
Chunk positions refer to lines of the original file, not of the output after earlier chunks.

Applying an Update rereads the file, applies chunks in original-index order, rejects a chunk that starts inside an earlier chunk's deletions as overlapping, copies untouched and inserted lines without indentation changes, and joins lines with LF plus a final newline unless the original and the result are both empty.

Each chunk's deleted lines must equal the file lines at its index after whitespace stripping, or the Update fails with "Mismatch applying patch near line <n>" listing expected and found lines, while surrounding context is not rechecked.
An Update whose file is missing or unreadable at application fails with "UPDATE Error: File does not exist" or "Could not read file for UPDATE".
An Add whose path existed before the reply fails with "ADD Error: File already exists: <path>".
An Add prints "Adding <path>", creates parent directories, and writes its content with a trailing newline.
A Delete prints "Deleting <path>" and removes the file, or warns "DELETE Warning: File not found, skipping" when the file is already gone.

An Update with Move to prints "Updating and moving <path> to <dest>", writes the updated content to the destination after creating its parent directories, warns and overwrites an existing different destination, and then removes the source.
An Add of a path that was missing before the reply writes its full content after the user approves creating it, instead of failing on the empty file the approval created.

fix.defect: Common authorization touches an approved missing file before application, so Add then finds the path, fails with "ADD Error: File already exists", leaves an empty file, still reports the path as edited, and the CLI --apply run exits 0. The reconstruction reproduces this with the shared-lifecycle probe and the real CLI (patch-lifecycle.json, cli-apply-results.json).
fix.intent: The patch prompt defines Add as creating a new file with the given lines (aider/coders/patch_prompts.py:153), the user approved "Create new file?" for that path (aider/coders/base_coder.py:2207), and the Add guard exists to protect files that already existed (aider/coders/patch_coder.py:567-569).
fix.behavior: Treat a path created empty by this reply's approval as new, so the approved Add writes its content with a trailing newline. An Add of a path that existed before the reply still fails with "ADD Error: File already exists: <path>".

rows.behavior: An Update with Move to writes its destination only after the destination passes the same approval as any other edited path.

fix.defect: Authorization sees only the source path of a patch action, so a Move to destination outside the chat is written, and an existing destination overwritten, without approval. The reconstruction lists this as a source-confirmed gotcha (aider/coders/patch_coder.py:583-634).
fix.intent: Every edited path passes allowed_to_edit, which asks "Allow edits to file that has not been added to the chat?" or "Create new file?" before Aider writes a file outside the chat (aider/coders/base_coder.py:2191-2240,2269-2294), and the patch prompt says "Only create patches for files that the user has added to the chat!" (aider/coders/patch_prompts.py:147).
fix.behavior: Authorize a Move to destination with the same rules as an edited path: no prompt when it is in the editable chat set, "Create new file?" when it is missing, and "Allow edits to file that has not been added to the chat?" when it exists outside the chat. A declined destination skips the action and leaves the source unchanged.

rows.behavior: Each request is assembled in the order system prompt, example messages, read-only files, repository map, chat history, editable files, current exchange, and reminder.

A format's example conversations are appended to the system prompt under "# Example conversations:" when the model sends examples as system text, and otherwise are sent as messages followed by a "I switched to a new code base" user message and "Ok.".

The format reminder is appended to the system prompt and, when the request fits the model input limit or the limit is unknown, also sent as a final system message for "sys" reminder models or appended to the last user message for "user" reminder models.
A request whose estimated tokens reach the model input limit reports the overflow with ways to reduce context and is sent only if the user confirms "Try to proceed anyway?".

Image and PDF files in the chat are sent as base64 data URLs labeled "Image file: <path>" or "PDF file: <path>" only when the model supports vision or PDF input, with read-only ones answered by "Ok, I will use these images as references.".

Reasoning text, whether from the provider's reasoning content or inside the model's reasoning tag such as <think>, is removed from the reply before mentions and edits are processed, and text before a stray closing tag is dropped.
Auxiliary non-streaming model calls, such as commit-message generation, return the reply text with the model's reasoning-tag content removed.
After a complete reply, edits are parsed, preflighted, authorized, and then applied, in that order, never per streamed token.
A format or application error prints "The LLM did not conform to the edit format.", the edit-errors URL, and the error text, and sends the error text to the model as the next request.
Every ValueError raised while handling edits counts as a malformed response, whether it came from syntax or from application.
A reflected message becomes the next request until none is set, and after the maximum number of reflections (three) the loop stops with "Only 3 reflections allowed, stopping.".

A reply that stops at the output limit without continuation applies no edits, records the assistant message "FinishReasonLength exception: you sent too many tokens" after a trailing user message, and shows the token-limit error.
An interrupted reply applies no edits and records "^C KeyboardInterrupt" on the user side and "I see that you interrupted my previous reply." on the assistant side of the exchange.
A reply that ends in a non-retryable provider error applies no edits and runs no follow-up from its partial content.

fix.defect: After a non-retryable provider error the retry loop breaks without an exhausted or interrupted flag, so partial reply content continues to mention handling and edit application. The reconstruction calls this a source-confirmed control-flow concern (aider/coders/base_coder.py:1446-1506).
fix.intent: The two other incomplete-reply paths return before edit application: output exhaustion (aider/coders/base_coder.py:1536-1547) and interruption, which records "I see that you interrupted my previous reply." (aider/coders/base_coder.py:1575-1583).
fix.behavior: When the provider request ends in a non-retryable error, show the error and do not process mentions, apply edits, commit, lint, run commands, or test from the partial reply.

rows.behavior: After application the exchange moves into chat history, followed by the commit message pair, or by the format's "I updated the files." notice and "Ok." when no commit was made.
In dry-run mode a SEARCH/REPLACE block that would create a new file is reported as "Did not apply edit to <path> (--dry-run)" without an error.

fix.defect: Dry-run approval skips creating the new file, so SEARCH/REPLACE application finds no file, builds a failure report from unreadable content, and prints "<path>: file not found error" and "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'splitlines'" instead of the dry-run notice. Reproduced against the pinned checkout with Coder.create(..., dry_run=True) and an empty-SEARCH block for new.txt.
fix.intent: The --dry-run help says "Perform a dry run without modifying files" (aider/args.py:512), and apply_updates reports each edit in dry-run as "Did not apply edit to <path> (--dry-run)" (aider/coders/base_coder.py:2330-2334).
fix.behavior: In dry-run, treat an approved new-file block as applying to empty content without writing, and report "Did not apply edit to <path> (--dry-run)" with no error, no file, and no reflection.

rows.behavior: An edit to a path already in the editable chat set is approved without a prompt.
When an approved new file cannot be created, "Unable to create <path>, skipping edits." is reported and the path's edits are dropped.
Authorization asks once per distinct path in a reply and keeps or drops every edit for that path by that answer, while records with no path pass through.

An edit to a read-only chat file is not refused: it asks "Allow edits to file that has not been added to the chat?" and, when approved, adds the file to the editable set while it stays in the read-only set.
A model-generated edit path is joined to the root and normalized without a containment check, so a path outside the root goes through ordinary approval and is written when approved.
A failing patch action stops application with "Error applying action '<type>' to <path>: <reason>", and actions applied before it stay applied.
The line-endings setting accepts platform, lf, or crlf, writing with the platform newline, LF, or CRLF, and any other value fails with "Invalid line_endings value: <value>" listing the three choices.

A confirmation shows the question with its subject and options, accepts any case-insensitive prefix of an offered answer, takes the default (yes) on empty input or end of input, and repeats "Please answer with one of: ..." on other input.
With yes-always every confirmation answers yes without asking except those requiring an explicit yes, which answer no, and with always-no every confirmation answers no.
A confirmation grouped over more than one item offers "(A)ll" (unless explicit yes is required) and "(S)kip all", remembers that choice, and answers the remaining items of the group without asking.

A confirmation that allows it, and every grouped one, offers "(D)on't ask again"; choosing it answers no and makes the same question with the same subject answer no without asking for the rest of the session.

Before each prompt the chat files are listed, read-only first: in plain mode one per line with "(read only)" after read-only paths, and in pretty mode as columns labeled "Readonly:" and, when both kinds exist, "Editable:".
Slash-command arguments complete from the command's own candidates, such as addable files for /add and chat files for /drop.
An edit to a gitignored path is skipped with "Skipping edits to <path> that matches gitignore spec.".
An approved edit path that Git does not track is staged with git add when automatic commits are on, whether it was just created or already existed outside the chat.
Before edits apply, approved target files with uncommitted changes are announced with "Committing <path> before applying edits." and committed when dirty commits are on.
Turning automatic commits off also turns dirty commits off.
A commit stages and commits the whole content of the named files, not only the regions the model changed.
Commit-message generation sends the commit diff and the chat context to the commit-message models.

Tracked files named in a reply but not in the chat are offered one by one with "Add file to the chat?", and when any are added the reply's edits are not applied and the model is asked again with the added files.
/add refuses a non-image file outside the root with "Can not add <path>, which is not within <root>" only while automatic commits are on.

/undo refuses without a repository, on the first commit, when HEAD was not made by pi-maintainer in this session, on a merge commit, when a changed file is dirty or absent from the parent commit, and when HEAD equals the local origin/<branch> reference.

/undo checks out each file changed by the last commit from its parent, aborts with lists of restored and unrestored files if any checkout fails, and otherwise soft-resets HEAD by one commit and reports "Removed: <hash> <message>".
Edited files are auto-committed before lint and tests run, so lint or test failures do not prevent the commit.
After edits apply, lint runs on the edited files when automatic lint is on, then approved suggested shell commands run, then the test command runs when automatic tests are on.
Lint errors ask "Attempt to fix lint errors?" and test failures ask "Attempt to fix test errors?", and a confirmed answer sends the errors to the model as the next request.
Automatic lint defaults on and automatic tests default off.

Python lint combines tree-sitter syntax errors, compile errors, and flake8 errors limited to E9,F821,F823,F831,F406,F407,F701,F702,F704,F706, reported under "# Fix any errors below, if possible." with tree context around the error lines.
/test runs the configured test command or callable and, when it fails, adds its output to the chat and returns it as repair context.

Each distinct suggested command block asks "Run shell command?" or "Run shell commands?" with an explicit yes required, runs each non-comment line in the root, and offers "Add command output to the chat?" for the collected output.
Shell, lint, and test commands run with the user's privileges, through pexpect when interactive on a non-Windows terminal and otherwise through a subprocess with shell=True.
